mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the unemployment rate above 8% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE > 8% for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, reducing earnings growth and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when GDPC1 declines > 2% over 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 2% signals a strengthening labor market, supporting earnings growth and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when PAYEMS rises > 2% over 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) above 1% signals improving manufacturing activity, supporting earnings growth and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when INDPRO rises > 1% over 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).
